# Vercode

> Ship better code. Catch bugs earlier.

## What VERCODE is
- VERCODE is the AI code review a team actually reads: deterministic static analysis runs first, task-routed AI reasoning runs on the bounded diff, and the result is published back to the pull request as a verdict plus evidence-backed inline findings.
- The VERCODE source is open under the MIT license. The hosted service runs on a publicly installable GitHub App.
- VERCODE analyzes code; it does not execute the pull request's own tests in the current release. The review pipeline runs in VERCODE's service; enterprise organizations can route model calls to their own providers via BYOK or a self-hosted Ollama deployment.

## Performance
- A review is published to the pull request in under 120 seconds at p50, from webhook receipt to GitHub publication.
- 95% of reviews are published within 300 seconds of webhook receipt.

## Pricing
- The Free plan costs 0 USD per month and is a permanent tier, not a trial.
- The Developer plan costs 24 USD per month.
- The Team plan costs 199 USD per month and includes strong-model access and 5,000 reviews per month.
- Enterprise pricing is negotiated per account; BYOK and Ollama customers fund their own model spend.

## Quotas and limits
- The Free plan includes 50 reviews per month.
- The Developer plan includes 500 reviews per month.
- The Team plan includes 5,000 reviews per month.
- A Team review processes up to 100 changed files; larger diffs degrade to the highest-risk files with a note.
- A Team organization can have 10 review jobs in flight; jobs beyond the cap are queued, not skipped.
- Findings below the confidence floor (default 0.6) are not posted by default; the floor is configurable per organization.

## Security and privacy
- VERCODE reads the pull request diff and bounded context; it does not store your source repository in its database. Findings are retained per the plan's retention window, then purged.
- The VERCODE GitHub App requests the least-privilege scope set: contents:read, pull_requests:write, checks:write, metadata:read, issues:read. It does not request admin:org or any secrets scope.
